clf-ini-001.text: Which of the following is an advantage of cloud computing compared with on-premises infrastructure?
options: Increased time required to provision new resources
A requirement to maintain long-term contracts with hardware vendors
Replacing capital expenditures (CapEx) with variable operating expenses (OpEx)
A need to purchase servers years in advance
clf-ini-001.explanation: One of the main benefits of the cloud is replacing large upfront hardware investments (CapEx) with pay-as-you-go operating expenses (OpEx), so you pay only for the resources you consume.

clf-ini-002.text: Which statement best describes the concept of elasticity in AWS?
options: The ability to encrypt data automatically
The ability to automatically increase or decrease resources based on demand
The ability to generate financial reports automatically
The ability to migrate data between Regions at no cost
clf-ini-002.explanation: Elasticity is the ability of a system to automatically scale resources up or down according to demand, helping avoid both wasted capacity and insufficient capacity.

clf-ini-003.text: What is an AWS Region in the AWS global infrastructure?
options: A geographic area that contains multiple isolated Availability Zones
clf-ini-003.explanation: An AWS Region is a geographic location made up of multiple Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone contains one or more independent data centers.

clf-ini-004.text: According to the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for security OF the cloud?
options: Neither party; it is the end user's responsibility
clf-ini-004.explanation: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud, including the physical infrastructure, hardware, and virtualization layer. Customers are responsible for security IN the cloud, including their data, configurations, and access management.

clf-ini-005.text: Which AWS service is used to manage users, groups, and access permissions for resources in an AWS account?
clf-ini-005.explanation: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is used to create and manage users, groups, roles, and policies that control access to AWS resources.

clf-ini-006.text: What does AWS recommend for securing the root user of an AWS account?
options: Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) and avoid using the root user for routine tasks
Delete the root user as soon as the account is created
Share the root credentials with the entire IT team
Use the root user for all day-to-day administrative tasks
clf-ini-006.explanation: AWS recommends protecting the root user with MFA, using it only for tasks that absolutely require root-level access, and using IAM identities with appropriately limited permissions for everyday work.

clf-ini-007.text: Which feature adds an extra layer of security to an IAM user's sign-in beyond a password?
clf-ini-007.explanation: MFA requires an additional authentication factor, such as a code generated by an authenticator application, in addition to the password, which improves account security.

clf-ini-008.text: Which AWS service is used for object storage, such as storing images and backup files?
clf-ini-008.explanation: Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) is AWS object storage. It is commonly used to store files such as images, videos, and backups.

options: A service that provides on-demand compute capacity through virtual servers
clf-ini-009.explanation: Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) provides virtual servers called instances that can be launched, resized, and terminated on demand.

clf-ini-010.text: Which AWS service lets you create a logically isolated virtual network for resources such as EC2 instances?
clf-ini-010.explanation: Amazon VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) lets you provision a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where you can launch resources in a virtual network that you define.
